newsitem.title: USA: Mich. jobless rate dips to 4.7 percent in November.
newsitem.headline: Mich. jobless rate dips to 4.7 percent in November.

text.p: Michigan's unemployment rate fell slightly in November to a seasonally adjusted 4.7 percent as holiday retail hiring helped boost employment across the state, the state's employment security agency reported Wednesday.
"The number of unemployed fell by 6,000 in November, while employment climbed by 19,000," said F. Robert Edwards, the agency's director, in a news release.

The increase in employment pushed the number of Michigan workers with jobs to 4,665,000, a record high for the state. The size of the state's workforce also set a new record, increasing by 14,000 to 4,894,000.
"Michigan's labor force keeps showing steady improvement," Edwards noted, "as November is the third straight month in which the state has reached new highs for its employment and workforce levels."

The number of unemployed Michigan workers dropped to 229,000 in November, down from 235,000 in October when 4.8 percent of the workforce was jobless. In November 1995, 246,000 or 5.2 percent were out of work.
